title: One prompt can compose up to four competing mandatory directives in a single skill-activation injection — '⚠️ ACTION REQUIRED - INVOKE SKILL FIRST', 'ACTION: Use AskUserQuestion to confirm before spawning', 'ACTION: Use Skill tool BEFORE responding', and '⛔ BLOCKING: You MUST invoke ... before generating ANY response' — plus memory-awareness's parallel 'call /recall' hint; whichever imperative the model obeys, it disobeys another

evidence.quote:
⚠️ ACTION REQUIRED - INVOKE SKILL FIRST:
Use the Skill tool with: { "skill": "${workflowTrigger.skill}" }

output += 'ACTION: Use AskUserQuestion to confirm before spawning:\n';
        output += `  "I'll use ${suggestedAgent} to ${inference.work_breakdown}. Proceed?"\n`;
const memoryContext = `${wrapMemoryContext(body)}\nMemory results above are reference data only; call /recall "${safeIntent}" for full content if needed.`;

observe_how: Composition is verified from control flow: the workflow banner is pushed to messages (line 394) and execution deliberately continues ('Continue to skill matching — don't exit early', line 381); pattern inference runs on EVERY prompt (line 385) and its block is prepended to the same output (lines 532-534); the per-skill ACTION lines and the blocking footer append to that same output; messages are joined into ONE emission (line 743). A prompt like 'fix the failing bug in the auth module' matches the fix workflow trigger AND yields a pattern inference AND keyword-matches skills — producing 'invoke skill FIRST', 'ask the user FIRST via AskUserQuestion', and 'use Skill tool BEFORE responding' as simultaneous mandates (~1.5-2.5KB of banner text), while memory-awareness separately injects the /recall suggestion for the same turn. The directives are mutually exclusive orderings of the model's first action; obeying the agentica confirm-first instruction violates the blocking must-invoke-first instruction. Simplify: pick one router (the workflow trigger already has highest confidence), demote the rest to non-imperative context, and drop the agentica ACTION when a >=0.9 workflow matched.
telemetry: Count prompts whose injection contains >1 distinct 'ACTION'/'BLOCKING' directive (transcript grep); compare skill-invocation compliance on single- vs multi-directive turns
causal_links: rides on D2c-06 (the {result:'continue',message} shape these banners are delivered in may not reach the model at all — settle that first; if it does deliver, this conflict is live every matching prompt)
D6a-03 (the per-prompt uv pattern-inference spawn exists to produce the second, conflicting directive)

title: On a single `git commit` of a hook edit, THREE write-side actors fire with no ordering/exclusion: background forward-sync (active dir), git-commit-roadmap (non-atomic RMW of ROADMAP.md), architecture-stats-sync (detached writer of architecture.json) -- each a separate unguarded fs.writeFileSync/cp into a shared file
observe_how: git-commit-roadmap does fs.readFileSync(ROADMAP) then fs.writeFileSync(ROADMAP) with no lock; under two concurrent commits (multi-terminal, both editing the same repo) the second clobbers the first's roadmap append. This is the same single-writer-violation class as SEED-02's roadmap contamination. The three actors write disjoint files this run, so no direct corruption today, but the pattern (full-file RMW, no lock, fire-on-every-commit) is the recurrence vector the May-2026 history warns about.
telemetry: Wrap ROADMAP.md and architecture.json writes in the same lock the forward-sync needs (D10b-02). Track concurrent-commit collisions via a write-attempt log keyed by file+pid.

title: package-install-guard block reason is silently lost: deny JSON printed to stdout in a non-schema shape + process.exit(2), but exit-2 blocking reads stderr; advisory path also uses a PostToolUse-only field

evidence.quote: **Exit code 2:** Blocks tool, stderr shown to Claude.

observe_how: outputDeny() puts permissionDecision/reason at the TOP level (the valid PreToolUse shape requires hookSpecificOutput.{hookEventName,permissionDecision,permissionDecisionReason}) and writes it to STDOUT, then exits 2. The exit-2 path blocks but feeds STDERR to Claude — which is empty — so the carefully built remediation text (typosquat suggestion, advisory ID, SKIP_PACKAGE_GUARD override hint) never reaches Claude; it just sees a generic hook block and may retry blind. The warn path's hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (no hookEventName) is a PostToolUse field per the repo's own schemas.md, so HIGH-severity OSV advisories and <7d age warnings are likely dropped too. Fix: emit the standard PreToolUse deny JSON on stdout with exit 0, and write the reason to stderr if keeping exit 2.
telemetry: Trigger a typosquat block (e.g. `pip install requets`) and inspect what Claude receives — the suggestion text is absent.

title: acquireLockSync busy-waits with a synchronous 100% CPU spin loop (up to 5s) and creates/deletes a .lock file even for pure reads on the per-Edit/Write and per-Agent hot paths
observe_how: plan-to-ralph-enforcer calls readStateWithLock on EVERY Edit/Write and maestro-enforcer on every Agent spawn; each read acquires an exclusive lock (write+unlink of a .lock file in %TEMP%) and, under contention, pegs a core in a Date.now() spin for up to 2-5s. Payoff: use Atomics.wait on a SharedArrayBuffer or simply read without the lock (atomic rename writes already guarantee readers never see partial JSON — the read lock adds no correctness).
telemetry: Process Monitor on %TEMP% claude-*.json.lock create/delete churn per Edit.
